serp_review.query: gmail mobile vs desktop bulk delete which is faster
serp_review.observation: Results included mailtrack.email (Mass Delete Gmail Emails 2026 guide), fyxer.com (two deletion guides), debounce.com, techloy.com, howtodelete.it.com, popsci.com (a Gmail speed tip, off-intent) and two auto-generated-looking pages on cloud.motorsport.unibo.it. Snippets agreed that desktop suits large deletions, but none gave a step count or a side-by-side capability comparison. Some contradicted each other or Google's help: one said the app forces tapping each avatar beyond 50, another said you keep scrolling. One vendor claimed 'less than a minute' without a measurement. None showed a head-to-head timing test.
serp_review.limitation: One standard US web search. Result pages weren't opened, so this characterisation rests on titles and snippets only.

information_gain: A side-by-side capability table (selection scope, all-matching action, search guidance, single-message triage, Trash, extension availability) for Gmail desktop versus both Gmail apps, plus an action-count table derived from Google's documented steps. The desktop count stays at 3 actions at any size, while the app count is 2*ceil(N/50)+1 (e.g. 41 actions for 1,000 emails, 201 for 5,000). This replaces the SERP's unmeasured 'desktop is faster' claims with a transparent, checkable basis and a size-based handoff rule (size the search on the phone, delete on desktop). It's framed as a decision page, not a device procedure.
overlap_check: Unpublished sibling drafts how-to-bulk-delete-emails-gmail-iphone and how-to-bulk-delete-emails-gmail-android each have a rounds table (Select all taps by count) and a short 'when to switch to a computer' section. This page overlaps them on the 50-batch fact. It differs in intent (choosing a device rather than following steps), in covering both apps against desktop in one capability matrix, and in counting total actions on both surfaces rather than taps on one. Pending gmail-select-all-conversations-desktop-site-mobile (browser desktop mode on a phone) and gmail-cleaner-wrong-device (extension on phones) are adjacent. This draft makes no claim about desktop mode in a mobile browser, and it gives the extension point a single FAQ line. Published how-to-bulk-delete-gmail-emails has a one-FAQ Android aside. A reviewer could reasonably decide this comparison belongs as a section in the hub or in the device drafts. The case for a standalone URL is the distinct comparative query and the two-surface action table. If the device drafts are published first, the reviewer should add links to them from this page.
limitations: Source and documentation review only. No live mailbox test on any device, no original screenshots.
'Faster' is expressed as a count of documented actions, not a measured time. Load time, scrolling distance and Gmail processing time for large selections are ignored.
The fetch tool summarised the pages. Quoted phrases were returned verbatim, but exact current app labels should be confirmed on the live pages or a device.
That the apps lack an all-matching selection is reported as 'not described in Google's help', not as tested absence. Whether an app keeps a selection across 100 Select all rounds wasn't tested.
The desktop 2-3 action figure assumes the select-all link appears when matches exceed one page, as documented; page size depends on the user's settings.
Which search operators work in the mobile apps beyond Google's app examples was not verified.
The cross-device Trash FAQ relies on both surfaces being the same account and doesn't cite a specific Google sync statement.
The SERP review relied on result titles and snippets, not opened pages.
